questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
As I wrote my Master Thesis this summer, I was in need of a change of scenery. I have always wanted to ameliorate my french, and Geneva thus seemed like a good match. 
Moreover, as I researched the leve at the University, it seemed to offer a serious level of education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Even though there was slight mismanagement between UoC and UoG, it all worked out fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most importance assistance was UoG providence of housing foras. That was crucial in order for me to go, as I hereby managed to get proper housing for student prising.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The one major issue – which is rather serious – is the long wait for getting documents approved. I know many that consider exchange, but backs out in the end simply because it seems to stressful. My own experience, writing a Master Thesis concomitantly, was that the approved of courses was an unpleasant experience to say the least. Never knowing when (and if) you are getting an answer is not up to what I consider the standard at the leading university in Denmark.

questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.answer: Explained above

questions.answer: It is just like living of campus in CPH

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It is very long ago so I do not recall the process in detail. 
However, unlike most other universities, you apply for courses after arriving during the first two weeks of the semester. This model has pros and cons

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Our studen advisor did a very good job at helping us out (Arnaud)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Everything worked out as I planned with slight modiration, as one course, which was approved on my preliminary study plan, apparantly was inavailable for exchange students. I was therefore forced to change my study plan.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talkwith someone who has been through the process before.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Tough the level varied among the different courses, I was overall satisfied with the level of the classes I attended - similar to UoC

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar - however the examination was much more thorough including both presentations, co-tutoring of classes, group assignments, individual essays. This was a VERY big plus which UoC could learn from.

questions.answer: I mentioned that already

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Exchange broadens your horizon. It is an absolut necessity for young Danish student to encounter the empowerment of inter-cultural experiences. Through this process, you not only obtain knowledge about other (exciting) cultures, but you also learn to understand what characterises your own.  Moreover, improving languages – in my case French and English – is pivotal if one seeks an international career, and on a personal level as one becomes better in navigating in the mighty world.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready for more exams than you're used to.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Revitalising my joy for academia

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Experiencing how difficult it is to learn a new language.
